construction: 55 parts in 1 step: two 8×8 and three 6×6 corner-cut plates, a 4×6 and a 4×4 corner-cut plate and a 6×12 plate overlapped into a swept trapezoid, two 4×4 wings with cutout at the tip, 1×4 and 1×6 tiles along the trailing edge, three 2×4 and two 2×1 curved-top bricks in red along the leading edge, two 3700 Technic bricks, two 60478 handle plates and two 61252 clip plates at the root, a grille tile vent and a 1×1 plate as the tip light.
interfaces: All studs up. The root Technic bricks' pin holes, the handle plates and the clip plates meet the fuselage frame; the plates' studs carry the parent's upper skin.
lesson: A studs-up delta wing from corner-cut plates (8×8, 6×6, 4×6 and 4×4 without corners) overlapped two deep, tiles along the trailing edge, red curved-top bricks as the leading-edge fairing, and two 1×2 Technic bricks with handle and clip plates at the root as the fuselage interface.
parent_context: `5892 - Airplane.ldr` places it at (−90, −40, −120) with the identity matrix; the right wing is a separate mirrored section at +Z.
reuse_notes: Use it for any swept plate wing: overlap corner-cut plates so every seam is bridged by the layer above, tile the trailing edge, fair the leading edge with curved bricks and give the root a Technic-brick spar for pins.
